Subject: Post-demo: context-window qualification & model recommendations

Hi Emily — thanks again for the demo time today. Quick written recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth.

Call summary (high level)
- Goal: surface entire patient visit history (up to ~25k tokens) and generate structured visit summaries + problem list.
- Key constraints: (1) some patients have very long note histories, (2) latency target ~700ms per summarize request, (3) PII redaction required at ingest.

Observations from the session
- Example doc we looked at (20–28k tokens) loses context parts when using default endpoints. Truncation was visible in the generated problem list.
- You emphasized fidelity over extreme compression — prefer missing fewer prior diagnoses even if output is slightly longer.

Proposed immediate next steps
1) We’ll run a short qualification eval against a 200-sample set you’ll provide (de-identified excerpts covering short/medium/long histories). Ideal split: 80 short (<2k tokens), 80 medium (2–8k), 40 long (>12k).
2) Redwood will return: (a) candidate model matrix (latency / cost / quality estimates), (b) a prompt-suite (starter prompts and instruction templates), (c) benchmark outputs and truncation diagnostics.
3) Pilot SOW: 4-week pilot to validate fidelity & latency at scale (we attach a starter SOW template).

Immediate asks for Chartly Health
- Can you confirm the de-identified sample export and expected delivery by EOD Tue (Jan 12)? If not, what date works?
- Any strict constraints on tokenization (we assume UTF-8, typical wordpiece)?

Attachments we will provide in the follow-up: redwood-long-window-benchmarks.pdf (summary of past long-window results), prompt-suite-v1.jsonl (starter prompts), pilot-sow-template.docx

Thanks — looping Neha for data coordination and Karthik for the evaluation plan.

Best,

Thanks Logan — this is helpful. A few clarifying items from our side:

1) Sample delivery: we can deliver an initial batch of 150 de-identified records by Jan 13; pushing to 200 will be tight because of downstream approvals. Is 150 still workable?
2) Edge cases: we have many threaded notes where the most recent problem list is split across multiple messages — will the eval plan consider inter-note threading?
3) Redaction: we have a PII scrubber but it occasionally leaves free-text initials; we need the model to not hallucinate full names from initials.

On the model side we care about: preservation of historical diagnoses, not inventing dates, and clear provenance markers ("based on notes from 2024-03-..." etc). Latency target is firm for interactive triage.

One more ask — do you have any public benchmark examples specifically measuring truncation-induced label drop (i.e., diagnosis missing because earlier notes were truncated)? A concrete artifact helps us justify the pilot internally.

Thanks,
Emily
Director of Clinical Product | Chartly Health
emily.zhang@chartlyhealth.com

Subject: Re: Post-demo: context-window qualification & model recommendations

Emily — good questions. Answers + concrete plan below.

1) 150 samples is fine for the qualification run. We recommend the distribution: 80 short / 50 medium / 20 long for the first pass; we can expand later.

2) Inter-note threading: yes — our ingestion pipeline preserves explicit message boundaries and we include a threaded-prefix marker in the inputs so the model sees speaker/section delimiters. That helps reduce cross-message hallucinations. We will include a small ablation that flattens threads to show the effect.

3) Hallucination from initials: we’ll add a prompt-level safety instruction to disallow name expansion — e.g., "If only initials or unclear references are present, output '[redacted]' rather than guessing a name."

Model recommendations (qualification stage) — tradeoffs noted:
- option A: Llama3-70B-quantized (fast with Redwood kernels, expected median latency ~520ms on our dedicated pools at your target batch size; high long-context retention with prefix-KV streaming). Good baseline for fidelity/cost.
- option B: RedBench-XL (open variant tuned for clinical summarization, slightly slower ~680ms, better factuality on long docs in our internal benchmarks).
- option C: Retrieval-augmented LLM (baseline LLM 13B plus vector store context for very long timelines) — best for strict provenance but adds complexity and ~120–240ms extra latency per call.

We’ll run the 150-sample qualification across A/B (A vs B) + a small Retrieval-augmented probe on 20 longest records. Output artifacts we’ll share:
- per-record truncation map (what token ranges were used and where outputs dropped items)
- F1 on a small labeled diagnosis set (we can do a lightweight label job for 50 records if you approve)
- prompt-suite-v1.jsonl (starter prompts with safety & provenance instructions)
- redwood-long-window-benchmarks.pdf (summary and perf curves)
